topic_en: Why deploys lose or repeat background jobs (and 4 fixes)

linkedin.title: Why deploys lose or repeat background jobs (and 4 fixes)
linkedin.body:
Two things go wrong with background jobs during a deploy:
1) Mixed versions: new code sends a job an old worker can't read.
2) Duplicate effects: a worker charges a card, crashes before recording "done", and the retry charges again.

Graceful shutdown helps planned deploys, but it doesn't fix either.

What the public playbooks (AWS, GitLab, Sidekiq, Temporal) converge on:
• Deploy support before behavior: workers that read old + new first, producers second
• Put a version on every job; route incompatible ones to separate queues
• Give every operation a stable ID, and skip it on retry if it's already done
• Assume at-least-once, and keep old workers until old jobs drain

Versioning stops incompatible execution. Idempotency stops repeated effects. You need both.

How does your team deploy workers?
